subject.title: fix(msteams): avoid memory spikes from oversized certificate files

question: What maximum certificate-bundle size should Microsoft Teams authentication intentionally support while preventing unbounded local reads?
rationale: Azure Identity does not publish a 64 KiB limit, so choosing the permanent cutoff balances memory hardening against compatibility for existing certificate-plus-chain bundles and requires owner intent.

options.title: Use a broader documented bound
options.body: Select a generous evidence-backed maximum, enforce it with a truly bounded descriptor read, and document/test the supported certificate bundle shape.

options.title: Standardize on 64 KiB
options.body: Keep the proposed cutoff only with explicit owner acceptance, upgrade proof, and user-facing documentation of the new startup failure.

recommendation.title: Use a broader documented bound
recommendation.body: Select a generous evidence-backed maximum, enforce it with a truly bounded descriptor read, and document/test the supported certificate bundle shape.

likelyOwner.reason: HDYA introduced the federated certificate-authentication contract and is the strongest history-backed owner for its supported input boundary.
